question: Should OpenClaw accept this deny-over-allow exec approval contract now, including `tools.exec.denylist`, exec-approvals file/protocol `denylist`, SDK-visible denylist helpers, and interruption of `security=full`/`ask=off` execution?
rationale: The remaining question is not a mechanical code defect; it is whether maintainers want this persisted host-exec security policy and compatibility surface as the supported native contract.

options.title: Accept the contract
options.body: Approve the new denylist policy surface and merge after exact-head checks and normal security review.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep the runtime behavior but reduce or mark SDK/protocol exposure experimental before supporting it as stable API.

options.title: Pause for broader policy design
options.body: Hold this PR behind the canonical issue if denylist mode, path-deny overlap, prompt-versus-block behavior, or Control UI editing needs wider design first.

recommendation.title: Accept the contract
recommendation.body: Approve the new denylist policy surface and merge after exact-head checks and normal security review.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the gateway protocol, node-host exec docs, and native exec approval security surfaces.
